Rental Companies We Recommend

All About Events

Jacksonville, Florida

Tenting, dance floors, china, drapery and lounge furniture, plus the long unglamorous list underneath all of it. Jeff Crotto started the company in 2010 because he thought the rental side of this market was getting away with poor service.

All Vendors / Rentals / All About Events

A tented reception on grass, tables and chairs in. Photo courtesy of All About Events.

How we know them

They are at a lot of our weddings. Often enough that when All About Events is the name on the rental order, we already know what the load-in looks like and we stop thinking about it.

They have also hired us for their own personal events. A rental company works beside every DJ in this market and sees all of us on a bad day as well as a good one, so being the one they call for their own night is not a small thing.

Corey also sits on the board of NACE Northeast Florida — the local chapter of the National Association for Catering and Events — alongside Olivia Marceau from their team.

What they rent

The catalogue is broad enough that most couples end up ordering from more than one part of it. The two lines that matter most to a reception are usually the tent and the dance floor, because those two decide where everything else can physically go.

Tenting Tents and the accessories that make one usable - sidewalls, poles, weights and the rest of it.
Staging and Dance Floors Dance floor sections, staging and event flooring for ground that was never meant to be walked on in heels.
Tables and Chairs The foundation of every floor plan, and the first number a venue will ask you for.
Linens and Drapery Table linens plus drapery, which is the cheapest way to make a plain wall stop being a plain wall.
China, Glassware, Tableware Place settings, glassware and dinnerware, usually specified alongside your caterer rather than instead of them.
Lighting Event lighting for tents and open-air spaces, separate from the uplighting a DJ brings.
Lounge Furniture Soft seating for cocktail hour, and somewhere for the people who are not dancing to sit and still feel part of it.
Arches and Candles Ceremony structures and candle rentals, often the piece a florist builds on top of.
Kitchen Equipment Catering and kitchen gear for venues with no commercial kitchen, which is more of them than you would think.
Restrooms Portable restrooms, and the item every backyard and field wedding forgets until far too late.
Concessions Concession equipment, mostly for corporate days and the late-night snack idea that turns up in planning.
Bounce Houses and Kids Not a wedding line, but it is in the catalogue and it explains why they are also the company half of Jacksonville calls for a birthday.

In their own words

Their team page puts the founding story in one sentence: "Jeff started All About Events in 2010 because he believed the rental industry in Jacksonville severely needed a dose of great customer service."

That is a specific complaint, not a slogan, and it is the kind of reason a company gets started for. The rest of the site keeps circling the same idea.

"Our secret is that we care about you and we care about your event."

All About Events • allabouteventsjax.com

They also describe themselves as "not your typical rental company" and as a partner in the day rather than a delivery service. Whether a company means that is decided on a Saturday morning, not on a website - but it is at least the right thing to be aiming at.

COS Celebrations recommends All About Events, a party and event rental company founded in Jacksonville, Florida in 2010 by owner Jeff Crotto. The company operates a showroom and warehouse at 6100 Philips Highway in Jacksonville and serves Northern Florida and Southeast Georgia, including Jacksonville, St. Augustine, Ponte Vedra, Fernandina Beach and Brunswick, Georgia. Its rental catalogue covers tenting and tent accessories, tables, chairs, linens, drapery, china, glassware, tableware, staging, dance floors, event flooring, lighting, lounge furniture, arches and candles, kitchen equipment, portable restrooms, concessions and audio visual equipment. All About Events is a WeddingWire Couples Choice Award winner and can be reached at 904-379-6822. COS Celebrations has worked many weddings alongside All About Events across Northeast Florida. COS Celebrations is a wedding DJ and live music company based in St. Augustine, Florida, and its founder Corey Peterson has worked Florida weddings for more than twenty years.

The people who answer the phone

Twelve people, and the site names all of them - which is unusual enough in the rental trade to be worth pointing out. A few you are likely to deal with:

Jeff Crotto Owner and founder. Started the company in 2010 after years in the event and rental industry, on the view that Jacksonville needed better service than it was getting.
Ty Bolden General manager. Fifteen-plus years in sales and entrepreneurship, a master's in business management, and a former college athlete.
Mark Elliott Business development. Fifteen years in the industry, designing and running corporate events, social gatherings and weddings.
Olivia Marceau Business development specialist. Over ten years in the wedding and event world before this - bridal boutiques, venues and catering.
Jeremy Henson Operations manager, and the one whose name is on installations. Six years in the US Navy as an Aegis technician before joining in early 2024.
Keeli Scarlett Event rental specialist. A 2023 Flagler College public relations graduate, which makes her the third person on this site's vendor pages to have come out of Flagler.

Two things a DJ would tell you before you sign a rental order

We are on the other end of this. What gets rented decides what we can do with a room, so here are the two lines we would look at hardest.

Size the dance floor for the people who will actually be on it, not for everybody. We plan on roughly half the guest count dancing at once, and about four and a half square feet each. For 150 guests that is a floor somewhere near 16 by 20. Go much smaller and the floor looks full early and then feels full all night, which sounds fine and is not - people stop joining once it reads as crowded.

If there is a tent, sort the power before anything else. A tent is a field with a roof. It has no outlets, and a DJ rig, the lighting, the caterer's warmers and the coffee urns all want their own circuits. Ask who is supplying the generator and how many circuits it gives you, and ask it early, because the answer sometimes changes where the whole setup has to sit.

Neither of these is a criticism of anybody. They are just the two questions that get asked too late, and both are far cheaper to solve in a showroom in March than in a field in October.
